summary: The requested definitions are all present in dung-1995-argumentation.txt with clear page markers. The characteristic function F_AF is defined on page 8 (marker ===== PDF PAGE 8 =====) as F_AF(S) = {A | A is acceptable with respect to S}. The grounded (skeptical) extension is defined on page 9 (===== PDF PAGE 9 =====) as the least fixed point of F_AF, labeled GE_AF. The preferred (credulous) extension is defined on page 7 (===== PDF PAGE 7 =====) as a maximal admissible set under set inclusion. The stable extension is defined on page 8 (===== PDF PAGE 8 =====) as a conflict-free set that attacks every argument not in it. Links to nonmonotonic reasoning and logic programming appear on pages 8, 19-24, and 28-29: page 8 links stable extensions to stable models, Reiter extensions, and autoepistemic stable expansions; pages 19-21 show Reiter's default logic as argumentation with R-extensions corresponding to stable extensions; pages 23-24 show logic programming as argumentation with stable models corresponding to stable extensions and well-founded models to grounded extensions; pages 28-29 give a general method for argumentation-as-logic-programming. Page 18 provides the 'no bug if no stable semantics' result, and page 8 notes that stable semantics is not defined for every framework. The source text is fully available, so sufficiency is ready_to_synthesize.
